questions.prompt: Match each joint type to where it is found.
What are the functions of the skeleton? Choose all that apply.
options: Protecting organs like the brain and heart

questions.prompt: In the arm model, what happened to the triceps when the biceps contracted?
questions.explain: Antagonistic pairs: one contracts, the other relaxes.

questions.prompt: Why must muscles work in pairs?
options: Muscles can only pull, not push
questions.explain: Each muscle of the pair pulls the bone in the opposite direction.

questions.prompt: An adult has 206 bones and a newborn about 300. About how many bones fuse together as a child grows?
Explain why you can swing your arm in a full circle at the shoulder but can only bend your knee one way.
questions.modelAnswer: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint: the round head of the upper-arm bone sits in a cup-shaped socket, so it can move in almost every direction and rotate. The knee is a hinge joint, like a door hinge, so it only allows movement back and forth in one plane.
rubric: Shoulder = ball and socket, many directions

questions.text: A smooth, rubbery tissue called ___ cushions the ends of bones at joints.
questions.explain: The outer ear and nose tip are also made of cartilage.
